description: Game night with Robo, Duck and Bear: a big die rolls, shows its dots for a quick look, then hides. Kids learn to see 1 to 5 dots at a glance, that zero means none (a blank face, an empty bowl, a blank domino half), that 3 is still 3 in any shape, and the order 0 to 5 on a number path.

youtube.title: Dot Dice! Count 0 to 5 in One Look | Preschool Math | Toy Box Friends
youtube.description:
It's game night! Bear rolls a big dot die, Robo lets you take one quick look, then hides it: how many dots? Kids learn to see 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 dots at a glance (without counting one by one), that zero means none (a blank face, an empty bowl, a blank domino half), that three dots are still three in a row or a triangle, and how to put 0 to 5 in order on a number path.

Try it at home with a grown-up: draw big dots on six cards (0 to 5, in dice patterns). Flash a card for two seconds and say how many, then count to check. Move five big blocks or toys into new shapes: still five? Use big things, not small buttons, for little ones, and put everything away after.

Made for kids. Toy Box Friends: 3D learning videos for preschool.

do.text: I brought my big die. Here it comes!
Can you see it in one look? Four!
Not broken. That's zero! This is a special die.
Fun fact! On a normal die, opposite sides add up to seven.
Let's play quick look. Look fast, then I hide it!
One! You saw it in one look.
Two in the corners. Quick look!
Two! You saw it in one look.
Three! You saw it in one look.
Four! You saw it in one look.
You can see up to four things in one look!
Now add one more, in the middle!
Four, and one more, is five!
Show me five fingers! A high five!
No dots means zero. Zero means none.
Look in this bowl. How many cookies?
My domino has a blank half. Zero on top!
And this is how we write zero.
Show me zero. A closed fist!
Three dots, in a slanted line.
A long row! Now there are more dots, right?
Still three! Same number, new shape!
A number path! Zero, one, two, three, four, five.
Zero, one, two, three, four, five!
Zero, one, two, three, four, five! Bye-bye!
